A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STAR-Bench study. Their main text, figures, tables and appendices A–F are readable and can be matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 19 models, human baselines, error analyses and temporal/spatial ablations, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations, including Table 2, appendix Tables 4–6, ablations and case studies.

M1.justification: The benchmark tasks, synthesis and curation framework, segment-reordering procedure, and native/channel-wise input procedures are retained. Expanded curation documentation does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions report the same coverage: 951 foundational-perception, 900 temporal-reasoning and 502 spatial-reasoning questions, using the same synthetic and real-world sources. No evaluation domain or task is added.

E2.justification: Table 2, Tables 4–6 and the comparison figures retain the same evaluated models and baselines. Table 1's revised descriptions of prior benchmarks do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Task ranges, metrics, audio preprocessing, input settings and Appendix C's evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Newly specified annotation training and spot-check details document curation rather than establish a revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Both retain the 200-failure error analysis, perceptual sensitivity tests, temporal caption/uncut-audio ablations, spatial input ablation and Appendix F cases. Expanded discussion of Figure 8 does not add an analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix C retains cyclic option rotations, three temporal-order evaluations, the single-evaluation exception for GPT-4o Audio, and AA/ACR reporting. No uncertainty estimation or seed-reporting practice is added.

E6.justification: Experimental scores in Table 2, Tables 4–6 and the ablation figures are unchanged. Table 1 revises categorical comparison findings: MMAR and MMAU-Pro change from unsupported to partial/limited spatial deep reasoning, and MMAR similarly gains partial/limited multi-audio coverage.

T1.justification: The benchmark definitions and mathematical specifications are retained. Neither version introduces new or revised formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and conclusion retain the same audio-4D framing, benchmark contribution, 19-model evaluation and principal capability-gap claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.2.2 reframes channel-wise input as a diagnostic ablation instead of suggesting human-like interaural processing. Sections 4.1–4.2 add interpretations concerning training-pipeline limitations and perceptual-range deficits in the existing audiograms.

D1.justification: Expanded Appendix B.3 documents conservative automated filtering, written annotator guidance, 10 trial annotations, task-specific review criteria, expert arbitration and rejection, and a random 10% expert spot-check. These add operational detail to the previously outlined workflow; access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A.2 and Table 1 acknowledge limited spatio-temporal coverage in existing benchmarks and distinguish it from STAR-Bench's physical/causal reasoning requirements. The bibliography is unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify related work, spatial inputs and perception analysis. Appendix B.3 gains two subsections, appendix references are standardized, and the header changes from Preprint to Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026. The overall structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 1's symbols and legend change, Figure 8's caption now names range and sensitivity, and existing figures are resized or relocated, notably Figures 4 and 8–9. Appendix material reflows without adding or removing figures or tables.

improvement.justification: Appendix B.3 makes previously abbreviated annotation and quality-control procedures more assessable and reproducible. More qualified prior-work comparisons and clearer explanations of the spatial ablation improve the argument. The retained experiments and numerical results make this a limited gain in transparency and interpretation.
